references.text: Jesus finds the healed man in the temple. After the healing, Jesus actively seeks him out, just as he does in [ref:Joh 9:35|John 9:35], where he finds the man born blind after he had been cast out of the synagogue.
Jesus' warning "sin no more" (μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε) is nearly identical to his words to the woman caught in adultery: "go, and sin no more" ([ref:Joh 8:11|John 8:11]).

The connection between sin and sickness is addressed in [ref:Joh 9:2-3|John 9:2-3], where the disciples ask if the man born blind had sinned. Jesus nuances the relationship between sin and suffering there, but here in 5:14 he suggests that the man's illness was connected to sin.
In [ref:Mark 2:5|Mark 2:5], Jesus forgives the paralyzed man's sins before healing him, demonstrating the link between sin and sickness as well as Jesus' authority over both.

[ref:Matt 12:45|Matthew 12:45] tells of the unclean spirit that returns with seven others, and "for that person the last state is worse than the first" – a clear parallel to Jesus' warning that something worse may happen.

[ref:Hebr 10:26-27|Hebrews 10:26-27] warns that if we sin willfully after receiving knowledge of the truth, only a fearful judgment remains – a parallel to Jesus' warning that something worse may happen.

[ref:2 Pet 2:20|2 Peter 2:20] warns that for those who have known the Lord and then return to sin, the last state is worse than the first, thematically paralleling Jesus' words "so that nothing worse may happen to you".

In [ref:3 Mos 26:23-24|Leviticus 26:23-24], God warns that if the people do not turn back, he will strike them even harder – a parallel to Jesus' warning that something worse may happen if the man continues to sin.
[ref:Jak 5:14-15|James 5:14-15] links healing, prayer, and forgiveness of sins, showing the close connection between physical healing and spiritual restoration.

In [ref:Jes 1:5|Isaiah 1:5], the Lord asks why the people should be struck even more when they continue in rebellion, reflecting Jesus' warning about the consequences of continuing to sin after receiving grace.
